name: Coucou
cost: Free (MIT code). Chat features use your own API keys
works_with: Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Amp and more
short: A small companion in your Mac's notch, or the top of the screen on Windows and Linux, that shows your agent sessions and lets you approve them.
what: Coucou shows each coding agent session live: what it reads, edits and runs. Claude Code permission requests appear with Allow, Deny and Always, and you can answer its questions from the notch. An iPhone app and an Android app let you approve from your phone. Since 0.4 the Mac app also does dictation, call notes and a chat with several AI providers.
who: People who run coding agents in the background and want to approve them without switching windows. Most of the extras are Mac only, so Windows and Linux users get less.
needs: macOS 15 or later, Windows 10 or 11, or Linux
iOS 18 or later for the iPhone app, or Android 11 or later for the Android app
An Anthropic API key for chat, and other keys only for the services you add

steps.title: Then install the app
steps.text: Or download `Coucou.zip` from Releases, move Coucou.app to Applications and click Open when macOS asks.

steps.title: Or install on Windows or Linux
steps.text: On Windows, download the `.msi` or setup `.exe` from the README's links. On Linux, use the AppImage, or install the `.deb` with this command (the `.rpm` works with `dnf`).

steps.title: Install the hooks
steps.text: In Settings, click Install hooks. For Claude Code, Coucou backs up `~/.claude/settings.json`, merges its hooks and shows you the diff before it writes anything.

steps.title: Add your phone (optional)
steps.text: iPhone: join the TestFlight beta, turn on Settings, General, iPhone in the Mac app, and use the same Apple Account on both. Android: install the APK from the release page, turn on Settings, Android phone on Windows or Linux, and scan the pairing code on the same Wi-Fi.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Open Settings, General, Demo and click Try demo mode. It walks through a scripted session with no API key and nothing written to disk.

watch: It edits your agents' settings files to add hooks. It backs them up and shows the diff first.
You can approve agent actions from your phone. The iPhone app asks for Face ID on every Allow, and Android needs your fingerprint or screen lock.
The Windows installer isn't code-signed yet, so SmartScreen shows a warning the first time.
The WhatsApp pill is experimental and uses an unofficial gateway. The README warns that WhatsApp may restrict an account that abuses it.
The Notetaker records your microphone and what your Mac plays. The README says to tell people in the call that you are recording.
Flow dictation needs the Accessibility and Microphone permissions.
No telemetry and no account. Keys are kept in your system keychain.
